packets.title: Preserve the declared charset across continued IMAP attachment filenames
packets.owner: Root assigns one IMAP owner; this replaces the broad P057 MIME grant rather than creating a second package owner.
dependencies_satisfied: P056 completed output reviewed for this exact MIME scope
packets.existing_behavior_gap: normalizeParams decodes each continuation separately. Later encoded segments lose the first segment's charset, and a multibyte UTF-8 character split between pieces becomes replacement characters.

evidence.result: One control passes; three ordinary continued-name cases fail for both Content-Disposition filename and Content-Type name.
evidence.event_consequence: Statically traced to src/events.ts attachmentName; event-level test is part of implementation acceptance.

implementation_contract: Reassemble ordinary RFC 2231 continuation octets in numeric order and decode the complete value once using the charset declared in the first encoded segment.
Respect encoded versus unencoded continuation pieces; an unencoded percent sign remains literal.
Retain existing simple unencoded and single extended parameter behavior, existing charset fallback behavior, limits, and attachment reference policy.
Keep expected Unicode strings authored independently from the implementation; do not regenerate goldens from messageEvent.

normal_acceptance_cases.expectation: The same ordinary continued filename supplied in reversed parameter order has the same decoded name.
The same ordinary encoding cases work for a Content-Type name parameter through parseContentType.
An ordinary small multipart message produces a validated attachment reference named café.txt; message text, record ID and MIME section ID retain their existing contract.

Run the repository's applicable type/source/verification checks and the relevant non-live connector checks; preserve all failures and existing assertions.
Obtain independent review of the exact change before root integration; retain separate real IMAP qualification.

Mailbox connections or real FLAGS/UIDVALIDITY qualification

primary_sources.supports: Ordered continuation, one charset for the entire value, and mixed encoded/unencoded pieces.

packets.title: Cover expired Gmail history across a full-rescan reconnect
packets.owner: One named test owner under the existing P051 Gmail owner. Shared Google OAuth owner retains its reservation.
dependencies_satisfied: P050 history scope inspected against f57 and primary sync documentation
packets.existing_behavior_gap: Missing composed coverage of stale history rescan >20 items, reconnect/retry, completion into normal sync, and persistent gap diagnostics. Existing code implements these mechanisms separately; no production history defect was established.

evidence.kind: static source and coverage inventory only
existing_coverage: connector.test.ts:50 one-message missing GET and history expiry
live-retry.test.ts:50 one history response containing 25 items
evidence.do_not_claim: This task is not a source bug fix or full connector acceptance.

implementation_contract: Add only the new owned test file using the existing GmailFixture and the public connected/backfill/sync/close seams.
Use authored ordinary synthetic messages and exact event/identity/checkpoint assertions.
Exercise a full completed initial snapshot, an expired history interval, a multi-batch rescan with process reconnect, and the subsequent ordinary incremental change.
If a required benign assertion fails, preserve the failure and send the exact finding to P051; this test-only grant does not authorize a production rewrite or altered acceptance.

normal_acceptance_cases.expectation: Capture an ordinary 26-message fixture to completion and retain its cursor and event record IDs.
One previously seen message is absent during the gap, a surviving message has an ordinary label change, and the next history request reports expiry through the existing fixture.
The connector returns 20 surviving records with a new profile anchor, backfill phase, and history_gap_deletions_unreconciled; no absence-derived tombstone appears.
Close the instance, reconnect from persisted state, and retry the same input. Events and cursor match the first rescan output exactly.
Resume the returned cursor for the remaining five records; the accumulated rescan IDs equal the surviving fixture IDs once, phase returns to sync, and the gap diagnostic persists.
A later ordinary label change emits the expected existing record identity through a history request starting from the new anchor; the unreconciled-deletion diagnostic remains.

validation_required: Run the new normal-behavior test file and relevant existing ordinary history/snapshot tests in the real repository package environment, not a stubbed core.
Record exact base/change SHA, commands and exit status; run the repository's applicable checks for the final test change.
Independent review confirms a useful uncovered composition rather than copied fixtures or assertions generated from current output.

primary_sources.supports: HTTP 404 for an expired startHistoryId requires full synchronization.
History ordering, noncontiguous IDs, pagination and final response anchor.
